answer: Agents join only by burning a non-transferable "pearl" bond minted per hardware-attested island node: each island's TEE computes a unique enclave key per agent, and duplicate keys automatically void every bonded pearl. An attacker running N sybils must own N distinct attested devices and stake N full pearls, so identity cost scales linearly instead of staying near zero; slashed pearls fund saffron-weighted payouts to honest verifiers who report matching enclave keys, making detection profitable and forgery expensive.
